Subject: URGENT: sustained 5xx & 800ms p95 from us-west-2 — request immediate geo cutover

Neha,

We're seeing sustained 5xx rates (~4.7%) and p95 latencies spiking to ~780-850ms from our production traffic hitting us-west-2 beginning ~07:40 PST. Error traces attached (sverve_errors.log) and a Grafana snapshot attached (grafana_p95_spike.png). Our customers in North America are reporting timeouts and API retries.

Can Redwood initiate a cross-region cutover to us-east-1 now and drain the affected us-west-2 pool? Our SRE team is standing by to coordinate. This is impacting revenue and a live campaign. We need an approximate ETA for traffic steering and expected impact (any short-lived 5xx from drain step).

We are authorizing the cutover on our side but need Redwood's operational authorization and the specific step list.

Marcus

Marcus — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. I'm looping in Aditya (runtime) and Hannah (ops lead) to confirm the remediation plan.

High-level ask from us to you: please confirm that you authorize emergency geo cutover and that you accept the standard rollback/fallback policy (we may route a small fraction to a compatible model variant during transition). If you confirm, we'll proceed with the MAP below.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — immediate steps:
- 08:30: Rapid triage (runtime / logs) — confirm KV cache saturation and model variant health (Aditya)
- 08:40: Begin controlled drain of US-WEST-2 serving pool (no deploys) — traffic steering to US-EAST-1 with gradual 10/30/60% increments over 6 minutes
- 08:46: Monitor for 30s spike; if 5xx above 1% or p95 > 500ms halt and revert to previous steering policy
- 08:55: Once stable, complete drain and mark pool for post-mortem (no immediate scaling down)

Attachment: MAP-draft.md (draft checklist).

Two questions for your team now: 1) confirm authorization to proceed, 2) any compliance/legal constraints on rerouting that we should know about before we touch traffic.

Neha Kapoor

neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: sustained 5xx & 800ms p95 from us-west-2 — request immediate geo cutover

Quick technical notes from runtime:
- We see KV cache fill increase and a sharp rise in model KV eviction churn starting 07:36 — aligns with the Grafana spike. Memory pressure on the us-west-2 serving group is causing model shards to stall, producing transient 502/503 errors downstream.
- No recent model version rollouts in the last 24h; traffic pattern change appears to be client load spike + longer context lengths.

Recommendation: approve controlled steer to us-east-1. Steps I'll execute if authorized:
1) Lock model version on us-west-2 (prevent hot reloads)
2) Enable prefix/KV cache bypass for newest traffic (reduce cold-starts)
3) Start 10%->30%->100% steer over ~6 minutes using policy 'geo-cutover-quick-v2' (rollback threshold 1% 5xx or p95>500ms)
4) If we see transient 5xx during first 30s, pause and push to 20% hold window for 2m for circuit stabilization

Operational IDs and links:
- Runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-sverve-incident-pack
- Exec ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SVR-8421

I can start step 1 at Neha/Marcus authorization. Estimated time-to-reroute: 6–9 minutes end-to-end. Expected customer visible impact: brief increases in p95 for 30–90s, then stable.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

Exec summary and final confirmation:
- Action taken (23 Nov 2027, 08:40 PST): Initiated geo cutover policy 'geo-cutover-quick-v2' and steered traffic from US-WEST-2 -> US-EAST-1 in controlled increments (10/30/60/100).
- Observed: brief p95 blip to ~420ms and a transient 0.9% 5xx during the first 45s; stabilized to <0.2% 5xx and p95 ~140ms after full cutover.
- Post-action: drained serving pool in us-west-2 (no further customer impact), opened post-mortem ticket SVR-8421, artifacts pushed to runbook link.

Neha Kapoor — I approve the emergency cutover and close the loop here. Marcus, Hannah and Aditya are copied for post-mortem follow-up.
